admin_guide.title: WhiteDesk Administrator Guide
admin_guide.subtitle: Management Console, Features & Parameter Handbook
admin_guide.card1_body:
• Where to Configure: Triggered during initial setup by typing "admin <enterprise_key>" into the ticket message box.
• Parameters: Enterprise public key code provided by the licensor.
• How It Works: Once the code is entered, enterprise database tables are automatically provisioned, your device's public key is registered as the Global Administrator, and the organization's public key certificate is installed on your device.
admin_guide.card2_title: 2. Blind Identity Architecture & Zero Personal Data
admin_guide.card2_body:
• Where to Configure: 3-dot menu > Profile Desk.
• Parameters: One-way blind identity hash derived from the 12-word hardware security seed.
• How It Works: The system never requests phone numbers, email addresses, or real names from users or administrators. All operations run over blind identities, completely eliminating legal and personal data retention risks.
admin_guide.card3_body:
• Where to Configure: System architecture and ticket relay layer.
• Parameters: Ephemeral relay pool and local device storage policies.
• How It Works: During communication, ticket messages and attachments are held encrypted only temporarily in the relay cloud. As soon as they reach the recipient device or when the ticket is closed, transient cloud records are immediately and permanently evaporated; data is stored solely on the parties' local devices.
admin_guide.card4_body:
• Where to Configure: Main support ticket list.
• Parameters: Tickets with an empty assigned administrator ID.
• How It Works: Newly created unassigned tickets that have not yet been claimed by any specialist are marked with an orange cloud icon on the ticket card. When an administrator takes over the ticket, the cloud icon disappears and the ticket is assigned directly to that specialist.
admin_guide.card5_body:
• Where to Configure: Top-right 3-dot menu and Whisper tab inside ticket details.
• Parameters: "Take Over Ticket", "Change Unit", "Hand Over Ticket", "Close/Delete Ticket".
• Rules:
  1. Tickets sitting in the shared pool or assigned to another administrator only display "Take Over Ticket" and "Change Unit"; an unclaimed ticket never shows "Hand Over Ticket".
  2. An administrator can only hand over or delete tickets personally assigned to them.
  3. Internal administrator notes invisible to the end user are shared encrypted via the "Whisper" tab.
admin_guide.card6_body:
• Where to Configure: 3-dot menu > "Working Status".
• Parameters: "Available", "Off Duty", "On Leave".
• How It Works: The system does not automatically assign tickets to administrators whose status is "Off Duty" or "On Leave". Such tickets either wait in the shared pool with an orange cloud icon or are routed to on-duty administrators.
admin_guide.card7_body:
• Where to Configure: 3-dot menu > "Organization Settings" desk.
• Parameters: First response time limit and ticket resolution time limit (hours/minutes).
• How It Works: A countdown timer starts on the ticket card. When the limit is exceeded, the system alerts the administrator; to prevent tickets from remaining unanswered, the request is automatically returned to the shared ticket pool or reassigned to another available specialist.
admin_guide.card8_body:
• Where to Configure: 3-dot menu > "Provisioning Desk".
• Parameters: Administrators, Units, Applications, and Categories (4 core tiers).
• Stages:
  1. Tier 1: Add a new admin or edit their authority by entering their blind ID.
  2. Tier 2: Select the branch, unit, and applications the admin belongs to.
  3. Tier 3: Assign specific category permissions so the admin only sees issue categories matching their expertise.
admin_guide.card9_body:
• Where to Configure: 3-dot menu > "Approval Requests Desk".
• Parameters: Admin promotion requests, administrator removal, and unit/application deletion requests.
• How It Works: Critical operations are not applied immediately; they are placed in a security queue. No critical authorization or deletion takes effect unless a second approval is granted by the Global Administrator.
admin_guide.card10_body:
• Where to Configure: "Attach System Diagnostics" toggle when a user creates a ticket; "System Diagnostics" tab inside the ticket for administrators.
• Parameters: Device model telemetry, network response status codes, recent action console logs, and stack traces.
• How It Works: When the user consents and attaches diagnostics, this telemetry is sealed with the administrator's public key. The administrator inspects the root cause on a single screen without bombarding the user with questions.
admin_guide.card11_title: 11. Remote Desktop Support & Automatic PII Masking
admin_guide.card11_body:
• Where to Configure: Ticket detail screen > "Remote Desktop" button.
• Parameters: Mutual encrypted peer-to-peer session approval and local masking filter.
• How It Works: A direct remote desktop session is established without external software. Password input fields and personal form data on the user's screen are automatically blacked out on the user's device; raw sensitive data is never transmitted to the administrator's screen. The administrator safely provides live technical support.
admin_guide.card12_title: 12. In-Ticket Voice Call, Push-to-Talk & Radio Broadcast
admin_guide.card12_body:
• Where to Configure: Phone and Microphone icons on the ticket header bar, and the "Start a radio broadcast" button on the home screen.
• Parameters: Direct peer-to-peer audio channel, 15-second self-destructing push-to-talk burst, shared emergency radio frequency.
• How It Works: When text messaging is insufficient, a direct encrypted voice call is placed. Push-to-talk audio bursts are permanently shredded from disk immediately after playback. Radio broadcasts let you announce to all field teams with a single tap.
admin_guide.card13_title: 13. Federal Data Harvest & FDH Audit Desk
admin_guide.card13_body:
• Where to Configure: 3-dot menu > "Federal Data Harvest" and "FDH Query".
• Parameters: Target administrator selection, user scope, standalone local database export.
• How It Works: To keep enterprise data sovereign without relying on third-party servers, all tickets, private whispers, and file attachments are harvested into a local database with a single tap. Even offline, the entire archive can be filtered and reported via the FDH Query screen.
admin_guide.card14_body:
• Where to Configure: 3-dot menu > "License & Subscription" (Exclusively visible to the Global Administrator; completely hidden from other users).
• Parameters:
  - Core Plan: Local on-device AES-256 encryption, end-to-end encryption, zero server data, federal data harvest, automatic on-device PII masking, blind identity protection, system and error diagnostics attachment, dual-approval authority queue, mobile and desktop clients, unlimited admins and users, category and organization management, file and screenshot attachments, advanced auditing and reporting.
  - Live Plan: All Core features plus remote desktop, in-ticket voice calls, in-ticket push-to-talk, and radio broadcast.
  - Billing Cycle: Monthly or Annual (20% discount) billing options.
admin_guide.card15_body:
• Where to Configure: Via the "wdrun admin transfer" command in the licensor management console.
• Parameters: Existing enterprise name and the new device's public key identity.
• How It Works: If a device is lost, damaged, or replaced with a new phone, the new device's public key is submitted to the licensor. Through this transfer, all historical tickets, departments, settings, and administrator privileges are rebound to the new device with zero data loss.

user_guide.title: WhiteDesk User Guide
user_guide.subtitle: Zero-Knowledge, Data Privacy & Encrypted Support Desk
user_guide.card1_body: WhiteDesk never asks for or stores your phone number, email address, or real identity details. When the app is first launched, a 12-word secret security seed is generated inside your device's secure hardware enclave. Your identity in the system is protected by a cryptographic blind ID that can only be resolved on your device. You can set and update your display alias anytime from the top-right three-dot menu.
user_guide.card2_title: 2. Connecting to an Organization & Opening the Support Desk
user_guide.card2_body: Type the enterprise public key code provided by the organization serving you into the ticket message box and submit it. Your device immediately and securely binds to that organization's support desk, loading its logo, authorized units, and departments onto your screen.
user_guide.card3_title: 3. Creating a Support Ticket & Step-by-Step Workflow
user_guide.card3_body:
Tap the "Create a new ticket" button on the home screen to submit a new request:

• Name Entry Rule: If name entry is enabled in the organization's settings, you may enter your name. If disabled by the organization, your name remains hidden and your ticket is processed anonymously.
• Unit & Category Selection: Choose the department or unit relevant to your issue (Hardware, Network, Software, etc.). Accurate selection routes your request directly to the right specialist.
• Subject & Description: Write a concise summary subject followed by a detailed description of your issue.
• Custom Enterprise Fields: Fill in any organization-specific fields such as device serial number or branch code if requested.
• Ticket Statuses: Your ticket progresses through Open (under specialist review), Answered (specialist replied), Resolved (awaiting your confirmation), and Closed (archived).
user_guide.card4_body: You can create tickets and write messages even without an internet connection. Everything you write is stored in your device's local secure storage. As soon as connectivity is restored, your data is automatically encrypted in the background and delivered seamlessly to the relevant desk.
user_guide.card5_body: Using the paperclip icon inside a ticket, you can take a photo directly with your camera, pick an issue screenshot from your gallery, or attach documents. Tap attached photos to zoom in full screen and inspect details. All attached files are encrypted before leaving your device.
user_guide.card6_title: 6. Automatic On-Device Masking of Sensitive Data
user_guide.card6_body: Credit card numbers, national ID numbers, bank account details (IBAN), or passwords typed into the message box are detected by local security filters before leaving your device. Sensitive data is never sent to the server in plain text; it is automatically masked with asterisks on your device to protect your privacy.
user_guide.card7_body:
You can use two real-time voice communication channels during support sessions:

• Encrypted Live Voice Call: Tap the phone icon at the top right of the ticket screen to start a direct voice call with the specialist. Once accepted, a direct peer-to-peer encrypted audio line is established between devices.
• Push-to-Talk (PTT): Press and hold the microphone icon on the top bar to record and send up to 15 seconds of audio. As soon as you release your finger, the audio is encrypted and transmitted to the specialist. Slide your finger away to cancel before releasing.
• Zero-Trace Audio Destruction: Transmitted push-to-talk audio bursts are never stored on any server. Once playback finishes, the audio recording is permanently shredded from both device memory and disk.
user_guide.card8_body: No third-party remote access software is needed for technical troubleshooting. Upon mutual approval, the specialist can establish a live remote desktop session to your device and perform technical repairs directly. Password and personal information fields are automatically blacked out on the specialist's screen.
user_guide.card9_body: When creating a ticket, you can optionally enable "Attach System Diagnostics". When enabled, technical status codes of recent actions on your device are encrypted and attached to your ticket so the specialist can diagnose your issue much faster. You may turn this toggle off anytime to send zero diagnostic telemetry.
user_guide.card10_body: A digitally signed cryptographic receipt is generated for every closed support ticket, proving that the request and all correspondence can never be altered retroactively. Furthermore, once the organization's retention period expires, the ticket's encryption keys are permanently destroyed from the device, rendering past messages unreadable.
user_guide.card11_body: Type a ticket number, subject title, or keyword into the search bar on the home screen to filter your list instantaneously as you type. Tap the clear (X) button on the right of the search box to reset the filter, or use the status pills below (All, Open, Answered, Resolved, Closed) to filter your requests with a single tap.
user_guide.card12_body: Once your request is resolved, you can rate the support you received from 1 to 5 stars and share your feedback. You can also use the QR code icon on the home screen to scan device, inventory, or ticket QR codes in seconds with your camera.

security_privacy.title: Privacy & Security Policy
security_privacy.subtitle: Zero-Knowledge Architecture & Cryptographic Transparency
security_privacy.card1_body: WhiteDesk never requests a phone number, real name, email address, or contact list access. Sessions are conducted via anonymous cryptographic identities (WhiteID and Blind ID) generated by secure hardware on the user's device. By architectural design, identifying a user in the physical world is technically impossible.
security_privacy.card2_body: All support tickets, messages, and file attachments (camera, photos, PDFs) are encrypted on the client device using AES-256-GCM and Curve25519 standards before transmission. Servers and databases only relay unreadable ciphertext blocks; even server administrators can never view message contents.
security_privacy.card3_body: Voice calls take place end-to-end encrypted directly over a WebRTC P2P tunnel. Push-to-Talk (PTT) audio bursts are sealed exclusively with the ticket key and permanently destroyed from RAM and storage immediately after playback on the receiving device.
security_privacy.card4_body: Symmetric session keys of resolved and closed tickets are permanently wiped (CryptoKey.destroy) from the devices' secure hardware keystore once the configured retention period (24 hours, 72 hours, or 7 days) expires. Expired data turns into indecipherable noise.
security_privacy.card5_body: For closed tickets, a Merkle Root Digest is computed from the chronological sequence of all message hashes. Sealed with the digital signatures of the parties, the .json Immutability Receipt serves as tamper-proof evidence that cannot be unilaterally altered by either the service provider or the user.
security_privacy.card6_body: WhiteDesk contains no advertising libraries, user behavior analytics SDKs, or data broker integrations. It is 100% compliant with Google Play Store and Apple App Store privacy requirements.
security_privacy.card7_body: Users can delete all local cryptographic keys from their device at any time by clearing the application data. Because no personal identity data is held in the system, deletion is completed cryptographically and instantaneously.

radio.user_permission_desc: Allow connected channel members to make general announcements and radio broadcasts.

closure.title: Ticket Closure & Resolution Confirmation
closure.description: Controls user confirmation of resolution and automatic closure timers when an admin marks a ticket as resolved.
closure.require_user_desc: Even if marked resolved by an admin, the ticket remains open/pending confirmation until the user confirms "Yes, resolved".
closure.auto_close_title: Auto-Close if User Does Not Respond
closure.auto_close_desc: If the user neither confirms nor disputes after a resolution notice, the ticket automatically closes after this period.

self_destruct.title: Cryptographic Data Destruction (Evaporation)
self_destruct.description: Permanently wipes encryption keys and message history of resolved tickets from devices after the specified retention period.

rating.title: Admin Rating
rating.description: Allows the user to rate the admin's service with 1–5 stars and feedback after the ticket is closed.
rating.instant_desc: Allows the user to submit a star rating and feedback immediately upon closure without a waiting period.

escalation.title: Ticket Response Time – SLA
escalation.description: If the assigned admin does not provide an initial response within this timeframe, the ticket is revoked and reassigned to the next available admin or returned to the pool.

proof_of_integrity.title: Proof of Integrity (Cryptographic Receipt)
proof_of_integrity.description: Generates a mutually verifiable mathematical closure digest on both parties' devices for every closed ticket.
proof_of_integrity.auto_download_label: Automatically download Integrity Receipt (.json) when ticket closes

user_preferences.title: Advanced Preferences
user_preferences.subtitle: Voice call, live radio, and receipt download preferences
user_preferences.voice_desc: Accept incoming voice call handshake notifications
user_preferences.ptt_desc: Use fast in-ticket push-to-talk voice communication
user_preferences.receipt_desc: Save the cryptographic integrity receipt to device for closed tickets
user_preferences.rd_desc: Allow the support specialist to establish a remote desktop connection with your approval
user_preferences.pii_desc: Payment cards, national IDs, IBANs, and secret keys are automatically masked before leaving your device (GDPR/KVKK Compliant).

remote_desktop.title: Remote Desktop
remote_desktop.description: Provides live screen sharing and remote click/scroll control with user consent.

pii_redaction.title: On-Device Automatic Data Redaction
pii_redaction.description: Masks personal data such as payment cards, national IDs, IBANs, and API keys directly on the device before tickets reach the server.
